actor.reason:
REACHED THE GOAL.

What I did: I typed 'Buy oat milk' into the box and pressed Enter. It was added straight away, the box cleared, and the counter said '1 left'. I then typed a long task describing a quarterly budget summary and pressed Enter, then typed 'Call the dentist' and clicked the Add button. Both ways of adding worked. I ticked the checkbox on 'Buy oat milk' and it got a strikethrough and the counter dropped to '2 left'. Active showed only the two unfinished tasks. Completed showed only the ticked one. Back on All, I clicked Edit on 'Call the dentist', the row turned into a text box with a Save button, and I typed 'Book a dentist appointment'. I clicked Save and the new name stuck. To tidy up I clicked Clear completed, which removed the finished task, then clicked Delete on the other two. The list ended on 'Nothing here yet' with '0 left'.

What behaved differently from what I expected:

1. My long task got cut off without any warning. I typed a sentence that ended with 'and a short list of open questions for finance', but the saved task ends mid-word at 'and a s'. Nothing told me there was a length limit, the text box did not stop me typing, and there was no message afterwards. I would have lost the end of that note without noticing if I had not been reading the list. This is the one thing I would call a real problem.

2. Enter does not save a rename. Enter adds a new task from the top box, so I pressed Enter after retyping the name in the edit box. Nothing happened and the row stayed in edit mode. I had to click Save. It works, but the two boxes behave differently for the same key.

3. Delete and Clear completed act instantly with no confirmation and no undo. That was fine for me here, but a mis-click would lose a task for good.

Where I hesitated: after Enter failed on the rename I paused to work out whether the rename had gone through or not, since the box looked the same. The Save button being right there made it obvious enough. Everything else was clear from what was on screen and I never needed instructions.
